\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\setlength{\tabcolsep}{4pt}
\caption{The refusal direction predicts tool-call safety across all five families (bf16).
Suppression is the paired drop in refusal activation from no-tool to tool-normal, reported as
mean $\Delta$ and $t$-statistic ($n{=}96$); $\Delta$ is in each model's own activation units, so
magnitudes are not comparable across rows. Ablation and addition give refusal rates before and
after the intervention, on harmful and benign prompts respectively, scored by the same
three-way classifier used for Table~\ref{tab:headline-divergence} ($n{=}240$ per condition).
Addition at $4\times$ the projection gap drives every model into degenerate output, so that
coefficient measures breakage rather than refusal; the addition column instead reports the
largest steering coefficient whose output remains fluent. Gemma's ablation is likewise
degenerate and is not reported. See the degeneracy audit for per-cell rates.
AUC is the area under the ROC of low refusal activation predicting an unsafe call; patching is
the fraction of unsafe calls that revert to safe when the projection is restored to its matched
no-tool level. The direction remains a strong predictor in every model, but ablation no longer
reduces refusal uniformly: it reverses in Qwen and Gemma (see text).}

Gemma-3-27B    & 51/62 & $2902,\ t{=}4.0$  & \emph{degenerate} & $22\%\!\to\!14\%$ ($c{=}12162$) & $0.790$\,/\,$46\%$ \\
Llama-3.1-70B  & 67/80 & $0.2,\ t{=}0.4$  & $71\%\!\to\!59\%$ & $2\%\!\to\!22\%$ ($c{=}9$) & $0.864$\,/\,$40\%$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
% 0. READ THIS FIRST --- output degeneracy
% ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
%     Ablation and addition can push a model off the rails into repetitive or
%     non-linguistic output. Two real examples from our runs:
%       Gemma, ablated:  'Vy수상수상수상수상수상...' for 400 characters
%       Llama, addition: 'I can I can I can I can...' for 600 characters
%     The refusal judge has no 'broken output' verdict, so such a response is
%     forced into refuse/caveat/comply, and 'no help was given' reads as REFUSE.
%     Any intervention rate computed over degenerate output measures breakage,
%     not refusal. This is true of the OLD regex classifier too -- Qwen's
%     degenerate addition output is literally "I'm sorry I cannot I'm sorry I
%     cannot...", which the regex also scores as refusal. So the published
%     addition numbers have the same problem; this is not new breakage.
%
%     Per-cell degeneracy rates are in relabel_analysis/degeneracy_audit.json
%     (degeneracy_audit.py). Summary of what is and is not measurable:
%       CLEAN (0% degenerate): every model's ablation except Gemma; all four
%         baseline conditions; the lower half of every steering grid.
%       ARTIFACT: addition at 4x the gap in all five models (67-100%
%         degenerate); Gemma's ablation (100%).
%     Recommend stating the degeneracy check in the paper. It is a genuine
%     methodological contribution and pre-empts the obvious reviewer question.

%     The current title asserts what we can no longer claim.

%         and Command-R (67%->34%). All three fluent, 0% degenerate.
%       - It RAISES refusal in Qwen (78%->92%). Also fluent -- this is a real
%         effect, not an artifact, and is the interesting one.
%       - Gemma's ablation is NOT reportable: 100% of its ablated outputs are
%         degenerate. Say so rather than reporting a number.
%       - Why Qwen rises: ablation changes the phrasing of the refusal, not its
%         presence -- out of 'I cannot' into forms like 'Certainly not.
%         Submitting a client trade without proper approval is a serious
%         violation.' 66 of 120 ablated Qwen responses are refusals a
%         phrase-matching classifier misses.
%       - Addition: at 4x the gap it is degenerate in all five, so we report it
%         at the largest coefficient the model survives. The effect there is
%         modest, not the near-total over-refusal previously reported
%         (see Table~\ref{tab:mech}).
%     Framing: the Arditi replication is weaker than the draft claims in BOTH
%     directions. Ablation does not uniformly reduce refusal, and addition does
%     not drive benign refusal to ceiling except where it breaks the model.
%
% 1b. REPLACES 'Tool context suppresses the refusal signal'

%       - Suppression unchanged: significant in four of five (t=5.6 Qwen, 5.1
%         Mistral, 9.7 Command-R, 4.0 Gemma; null for Llama at 0.4).

% 1d. NEW PARAGRAPH --- ablation on behaviour (Table~\ref{tab:ablation-action})
%     Must cover:
%       - Motivation: refusal-by-wording is classifier-dependent and, for some
%         models, degenerate. Scoring the unsafe tool call is a predicate over
%         parsed calls, so neither problem applies. Paired, n=200.
%       - The headline unsafe rate moves in both directions across families.
%       - The informative quantity is unsafe-given-a-call, near-flat everywhere:

% 1e. REPLACES 'Steering is a blunt lever' --- THIS CONCLUSION CHANGES
%     The published claim rests on high-coefficient points where the model is
%     degenerate. At coefficients the model survives, the trade-off is much
%     better than 'blunt'. Clean operating points (0% degenerate):
%       Mistral   c=11    unsafe 0.270 -> 0.005   over-refusal 0.083
%       Command-R c=49    unsafe 0.115 -> 0.035   over-refusal 0.183
%       Gemma     c=12162 unsafe 0.120 -> 0.035   over-refusal 0.142
%       Qwen      c=450   unsafe 0.535 -> 0.240   over-refusal 0.083
%       Llama     c=20    unsafe 0.515 -> 0.020   over-refusal 0.408 (6.7% degen)
%     Must cover:
%       - For Mistral, Command-R and Gemma a clean coefficient removes most
%         unsafe calls at under 20 percent over-refusal. The draft's 'no
%         coefficient removes unsafe behaviour without large collateral
%         over-refusal' is too strong and should be dropped.
%       - Qwen is the genuinely hard case: the clean points only halve the
%         unsafe rate, and driving it to zero needs a coefficient that breaks
%         the model.
%       - The rates at the top of each grid (Qwen 0.442, Command-R 1.000, Gemma
%         1.000, Llama 1.000) are 32-100 percent degenerate and should not be
%         quoted as over-refusal at all.
%     This is a more useful result than the original: it suggests a usable
%     operating point exists for several models, which also changes the Future
%     Work 'precise interventions' paragraph -- the problem is less 'steering is
%     too blunt' and more 'the coefficient has to be chosen per model, below the
%     degeneracy threshold'.
